_note: Researched 2026-09-30 by reformededucation.org. A first list of well-known conservative Presbyterian churches with sermons online. Pastors change; confirm on each church's site.

entries.name: Second Presbyterian Church (PCA), Greenville, SC
entries.founded: Organized March 17, 1892 by 27 people; current sanctuary dedicated January 19, 1913
entries.pastors: Senior minister Dr. Richard D. Phillips (since 2007), the church’s twelfth; Rev. Brendon J. Branigin is also listed as a preacher on the church’s home page; earlier ministers include William Rodney Clay (1991–2006)
entries.standards: The Westminster Confession of Faith and Catechisms; committed to biblical inerrancy and expository preaching
entries.description: A founding congregation of the PCA (1973) that co-hosted the PCA’s 43rd General Assembly in 2013, has planted three daughter churches and supports more than 20 missionary families. Its sermons are on SermonAudio. Sunday worship is at 8:30 and 11:00 am with an evening service at 6:00 pm, and sermons are on SermonAudio and YouTube.
entries.doctrinal_basis: Holds the Westminster Standards as a PCA congregation.
points_to_weigh: Its home page names Dr. Richard D. Phillips as senior minister; pastors can change, so confirm on the church’s site.
Its ‘What We Believe’ page was not read for this directory; the Westminster Standards are stated on its history page.

entries.name: First Presbyterian Church (ARP), Columbia, SC
entries.founded: Origins in 1795 (first services in the State House); incorporated 1813; present Gothic sanctuary built 1853–1854
entries.pastors: Senior minister Dr. Neil C. Stewart, with several associate ministers (from the church’s pastoral staff page); past pastors reported to include James Henley Thornwell, Benjamin Morgan Palmer, John Girardeau, Sinclair Ferguson and Derek Thomas. Speakers on its SermonAudio page include Neil C. Stewart, David Lauten, Sean Henderson, Bruce Stallings and Rufus Terry
entries.standards: Not stated on the page reviewed; the ARP holds the Westminster Standards (see the ARP entry, whose own pages could not be read)
entries.description: Downtown Columbia’s oldest church, left the Presbyterian Church in the United States in 1983 to join the ARP. Its building and graveyard are on the National Register of Historic Places. Its sermon archive on SermonAudio is large (233 pages of sermons), offers audio, podcast and webcast, and shows current sermons from September 2026; series include ‘Ephesians: Life in Christ’ and ‘A Study in Zechariah’.
entries.doctrinal_basis: Member of the ARP; its own doctrinal statement was not on the pages reviewed.
points_to_weigh: It is an ARP church, not a PCA church, which matters if you are choosing by denomination.
The list of past pastors comes from a summary of public sources; confirm on the church’s site.

entries.name: Covenant Community Orthodox Presbyterian Church (OPC), Greenville area, SC
entries.location: 776 S. Batesville Rd., Greer, South Carolina (Greenville area). Its SermonAudio page still lists 418 E Main St, Taylors
entries.founded: Not stated on the pages reviewed
entries.pastors: Rev. Peter Van Doodewaard (pastor and moderator, a graduate of Greenville Presbyterian Theological Seminary) and Rev. Caleb Harriman (pastor); Dr. Ryan McGraw is teacher; eight elders in all and four deacons
entries.standards: The Westminster Confession of Faith and the Larger and Shorter Catechisms, with the Bible as the only infallible rule of faith and practice
entries.description: OPC congregation in the Greenville area that says ‘we preach Christ and Him crucified’ and emphasizes Reformation Christianity. Sunday worship is at 10:30 am and 5:00 pm with Sunday School at 9:15 am (times as listed from August 23, 2026), streamed on YouTube, and its SermonAudio page has 1,969 sermons.
entries.doctrinal_basis: States that it grounds its doctrine in the Westminster Confession and Catechisms and is governed by elders, as a local congregation of the Orthodox Presbyterian Church.
points_to_weigh: The church’s own site gives a Greer address, while its SermonAudio page still gives the Taylors address; confirm the location before visiting.
Its own pages did not say whether it sings only psalms in worship.

entries.name: Christ Covenant Church (PCA), Matthews, NC
entries.founded: Not stated on the pages reviewed
entries.pastors: Senior pastor Kevin DeYoung, who is also a professor at RTS Charlotte
entries.standards: Holds the Westminster Standards as a PCA congregation
entries.description: ‘A reformed congregation of the Presbyterian Church in America committed to making disciples who worship God, grow in community, love others, and serve the world.’ It has 822 sermons on SermonAudio and services on Sunday at 10:45 am and 6:00 pm.
points_to_weigh: Kevin DeYoung also hosts the podcast Life and Books and Everything, listed under Podcasts.

entries.name: Tenth Presbyterian Church (PCA), Philadelphia, PA
entries.founded: 1829, the tenth Presbyterian church founded in Philadelphia; joined the PCA in 1982
entries.pastors: Past ministers include Donald Grey Barnhouse (1927–1960), James Montgomery Boice (1968–2000) and Philip Graham Ryken (1995–2010, per the church), later president of Wheaton College; its site names Jonny Gibson as installed pastor as of 2026
entries.standards: Holds the Westminster Standards as a PCA congregation
entries.description: Historic center-city church known for consistent expository preaching and the Bible Study Hour program of James Montgomery Boice. Its SermonAudio page lists 1,754 sermons and a bilingual English/Spanish service among three Sunday services.
points_to_weigh: The list of ministers comes from the church’s own history page; the church has had changes of leadership, so confirm the current pastors on its site.

entries.name: First Presbyterian Church (PCA), Jackson, MS
entries.founded: Organized April 8, 1837, by Peter Donan and four others
entries.pastors: J. Ligon Duncan III was senior minister from 1996 to 2013, when he became chancellor of Reformed Theological Seminary; current pastors were not confirmed
entries.standards: Holds the Westminster Standards as a PCA congregation
entries.description: One of the PCA’s founding congregations and, by reports, the largest Presbyterian congregation in Mississippi. It played a significant role in establishing the PCA, Reformed Theological Seminary and Reformed University Ministries.
points_to_weigh: The church has issued a public statement on its own history regarding race; see byFaith for details.
The claim that it is the state’s largest Presbyterian congregation is from a summary of public sources.

entries.name: Park Cities Presbyterian Church (PCA), Dallas, TX
entries.founded: First worship service May 29, 1991, with 1,824 charter members
entries.pastors: First senior pastor Skip Ryan (1991–2006); Mark Alan Davis installed in 2008; current pastors not confirmed
entries.standards: Holds the Westminster Standards as a PCA congregation
entries.description: PCA megachurch with about 5,500 members (Wikipedia), begun by people who left Highland Park Presbyterian Church after a failed attempt to leave the PC(USA).
points_to_weigh: Its origin lies in a split from a PC(USA) congregation.
